title: Cause and Exit architecture audit
summary: Official-source audit selecting an optional binary semantic Cause and Exit model without changing generic Result.

payload.question: Should ResultSafe define optional portable Cause<E> and Exit<T,E> models, and which topology and compatibility boundary should they use?
methodology: Inspect official language, runtime, and project documentation and record only directly documented public behavior
Keep direct source observations separate from ResultSafe interpretation and known limitations
Score explicit options against weighted ResultSafe criteria whose weights total 100
Treat scoring as transparent decision support rather than proof or source authority

official_source_practices.observation: Cause documents Empty, Fail, Die, Interrupt, Sequential, and Parallel cases for typed errors, defects, interruption, and composition.
Exit documents Success carrying a value and Failure carrying a Cause.
Sandboxing exposes the complete Cause in the typed error channel and unsandbox restores it.
ZIO Cause preserves typed failure, defects, interruption, and sequential or parallel composition.
ZIO Exit describes an effect result as Success or Failure with a Cause.
Outcome distinguishes Succeeded, Errored, and Canceled terminal outcomes.
Result is Ok(T) or Err(E), preserving independently selected generic success and error values.
Error source returns an optional lower-level error source and does not define parallel topology.
std::expected represents either an expected T value or an unexpected E value.
Swift Result has success and failure cases and constrains the caller-selected Failure type to Error.
Kotlin Result encapsulates a successful value or a Throwable failure.
CompletionException is an exception wrapper whose documented constructors can retain an underlying cause.
Throwable exposes one cause and a list of suppressed exceptions in addition to message and stack trace data.
Exception.InnerException retrieves the exception that caused the current exception when one is supplied.
AggregateException consolidates multiple failures and exposes them through InnerExceptions.
Python raise-from explicitly sets exception cause and exception context records implicit handling context.
ExceptionGroup wraps a non-empty sequence of exceptions and supports nested exception groups.
The Error options cause property associates an arbitrary cause value with an Error object.
AggregateError stores an iterable-derived list of errors alongside ordinary Error behavior.
Go errors supports trees through Unwrap returning one error or a slice, and traversal uses depth-first examination.
Concurrent combinators document waiting for multiple computations and cancellation behavior when peers fail.
Linked Erlang processes exchange exit signals carrying reasons, with trapping changing receipt into messages.

criteria.measurement: Preserves Result<T,E> and arbitrary existing E and T values
Represents expected failure, defect, interruption, and composition without flattening
Has deterministic language-neutral data and explicit codec boundaries
Supports acyclicity, bounded traversal, and safe defect or interruption payloads
Keeps simple Result usage unchanged and makes richer semantics opt-in
Adapts faithfully to documented effect-system concepts without claiming representation identity

costs: No portable topology for concurrent or runtime failure

benefits: Preserves generic Result and exact semantic topology
Supports explicit portable codecs and semantic adapters

costs: Breaks Result<T,E> and forces effect semantics on all callers

interpretations: Official systems repeatedly distinguish typed failure from runtime failure or cancellation, but use incompatible payloads and APIs
A binary Sequential and Parallel algebra preserves ordering and grouping without imposing n-ary canonicalization rules
Portable Die and Interrupt values require structured Failure payloads rather than runtime exception, fiber, thread, or process objects
Failure.causes is useful diagnostic ancestry but cannot preserve Cause sequencing or parallel topology
Semantic adapters can align meanings while wire formats, runtime identities, and APIs remain independent

conclusion.compatibility_rule: Result<T,E> is unchanged; Cause<E> and Exit<T,E> are separate optional models and preserve arbitrary E and T through explicit portable codecs.

limitations: Official documentation may change and this audit does not mirror external pages
Observed exception and concurrency systems are evidence of practices, not claims of representation equivalence
Weighted scores encode ResultSafe priorities and do not measure ecosystem popularity
JSON Schema cannot by itself enforce aggregate recursive depth, node count, or object-identity cycles; conforming decoders must enforce those invariants
